title: gov.uk Plan 2 interest page: at £35,000, £40,000, £45,000 and £52,885 the rate is RPI 4.1% plus the pay's share of the £23,500 gap times 3%: 4.82%, 5.46%, 6.09% and 7.1%, the last two capped at 6% from 1 September 2026
Plan 2, £50,000 owed, pay £25,000 below the £29,385 threshold for 30 years: nothing is repaid, interest compounds monthly at RPI 4.1% and £170,703.23 is written off
working: Pay never exceeds the threshold, so the repayment is 9% of nothing. The rate is RPI only, 4.1%, below the cap. Interest is added monthly: 50,000 x (1 + 0.041 / 12)^12 = 52,088.97 after year one, so 2,088.97 of interest. After 30 years: 50,000 x (1 + 0.041 / 12)^360 = 170,703.23, all of it written off; the interest is 170,703.23 - 50,000 = 120,703.23.

title: Plan 2, £5,000 owed at £60,000: £2,755 a year clears it in the second year, with £321.56 of interest, at 6% capped in year one and 7.1% in year two
working: £60,000 - £29,385 = £30,615; 9% = £2,755.35, rounded down to £2,755, so £229.58 a month. Pay is above £52,885 so the rate is RPI + 3% = 7.1%, capped at 6% in the first year: twelve months of interest at 0.5% on the falling balance come to £231.35 and the year ends at £2,476.35. In year two the cap has gone and the rate is 7.1%; the balance clears in the eleventh month, with £90.21 of interest. Total repaid 5,000 + 231.35 + 90.21 = 5,321.56.

title: gov.uk monthly example scaled to a year: Plan 1 at £33,000 pays 9% of £6,100 = £549 a year; at a flat 4.1% that never catches £20,000 of interest, and £31,780.11 is written off after 25 years
working: gov.uk's example: £2,750 a month - £2,241 = £509; 9% = £45.81, so £45 a month. The same income over a year: £33,000 - £26,900 = £6,100; 9% = £549, which is the page's own method for a Self Assessment year (its £42,000 example gives £1,359 the same way), and is what the model uses; monthly rounding would give 12 x £45 = £540. Plan 1 is charged 4.1% whatever the income, so extraMax is zero. Interest in year one on a balance falling by £45.75 a month: £825.15, more than the £549 repaid, so the balance grows every year. 25 x 549 = 13,725 repaid in all; Plan 1 loans first paid after September 2006 are written off 25 years after the April repayments were first due.

title: gov.uk Plan 2 interest example: £30,000 owed at £40,000 with no growth repays £955 a year at 5.455% and still owes £81,451.91 at write-off
working: £40,000 - £29,385 = £10,615; 9% = £955.35, rounded down to £955, £79.58 a month. The rate is 4.1% + 10,615 / 23,500 x 3% = 5.455%, under the cap. Monthly interest at 5.455% / 12 on a balance that starts at £30,000 and is reduced by £79.58 each month comes to £1,653.83, so the balance ends year one at £30,698.83 and keeps growing. 30 years of £955 = £28,650 repaid; the written-off balance is 30,000 + 80,101.91 - 28,650 = 81,451.91.

title: Plan 2, £53,000 owed at £35,000, pay up 6.1% a year, threshold frozen for four years then up 4.1%: the repayment reaches £1,238 in year five but £118,183.86 is still written off
working: Year one: £35,000 - £29,385 = £5,615; 9% = £505.35, so £505; rate 4.1% + 5,615 / 23,500 x 3% = 4.817%. Pay grows 6.1% each April: year five pay is 35,000 x 1.061^4 = 44,353.67. The threshold stays at £29,385 through years one to four (2026-27 to 2029-30, the announced freeze) and rises 4.1% from year five: 29,385 x 1.041 = 30,589.78, then 31,843.97 in year six; the interest thresholds move with it. Year five: 44,353.67 - 30,589.78 = 13,763.89; 9% = 1,238.75, so £1,238. The repayments never match the interest and the balance left after 30 years is written off.
